_comment: Shared by backend/tests/test_filename_title_parity.py and frontend/src/lib/__tests__/filenameTitle.parity.test.ts. `_filename_to_title` decides what a file is called before anyone renames it, and the search result row compares against that title to decide whether repeating the filename underneath says anything. Two implementations, one table. Several cases below exist because that is where the two languages disagree - a code point above the BMP, a trailing dot, and the whitespace `str.strip` and `String.trim` do not share - since a table of cases they already agree on cannot catch a drift. Non-ASCII cases carry a note saying what they are for.

cases.title: 𐐀ary
cases.why: U+10428 DESERET SMALL LETTER LONG I, above the BMP. `charAt(0)` returns a lone surrogate and upper-cases to itself; a code point does not.

cases.title: Notes.
cases.why: A dot with nothing after it is not a suffix, so the whole name is the stem. Pinned to the Python the backend image runs (3.12); CPython 3.14 answers 'notes', so this row is what would notice that upgrade.

cases.title: ﻿report
cases.why: U+FEFF: `String.trim` strips it, `str.strip` does not, so the first character to upper-case differs.

cases.title: Report
cases.why: U+0085 NEL: `str.strip` strips it, `String.trim` does not.

cases.title: SSeta
cases.why: Upper-casing one character can yield two. Both languages agree; pinned so a future 'optimisation' to charCode arithmetic does not.

cases.title: Istanbul
cases.why: Turkish dotless i. `toUpperCase` is locale-independent, so both give I; pinned because it reads like a place they would differ.

cases.title: 02 charon's burden
cases.why: `str.title()` upper-cases after every non-alphabetic character, so an apostrophe or a digit mangles the word after it.

cases.title: 6484215695 3df06f6b39 o
cases.why: Underscores separate; nothing after the first character is recased.

cases.title: MacBook-Neo-review
cases.why: An interior capital is the author's spelling. A hyphen is a character they chose, not a separator.

cases.filename: ヤンニョムチキン-韓国風-甘辛.mp4
cases.title: ヤンニョムチキン-韓国風-甘辛
cases.why: Japanese names never hit the `str.title()` mangling, which is why it went unnoticed. Pinned so the fix stays measured on both alphabets.
A name of nothing but separators has no title to make, so the stem stands as written rather than the row going empty.
